event_name: Ritual, Process, Becoming: A Conversation with Susan Cofer, Arthur Liou, and Morgan Bennett
blurb:
This one is for the people who think seriously about creativity, not just what artists make, but how they make it and what the process does to them over time.

The Zuckerman Museum of Art is hosting a conversation between artist Susan Cofer, KSU Dean Arthur Liou, and student docent Morgan Bennett about the rituals behind sustained creative practice. What does it actually mean to make work over years? How does uncertainty shape the outcome? How does an artist keep becoming instead of just arriving? These are the questions they're sitting down to unpack together.

It's intimate, it's substantive, and it's the kind of evening that makes you think differently about your own work, whatever that work is. If you've been meaning to spend more time at the Zuckerman, this is a good reason to finally go.
scoring_notes: Educated audience with cultural curiosity makes this a reasonable fit. The Zuckerman is a legitimate institution worth supporting. However, the topic is fairly niche and the panel format limits broad appeal. Lowest scored event in the set but still qualifies as a real, specific event during the window with clear demographic overlap for a segment of East Cobb readers.

event_name: Organ Recital: Andrew Van Varick
venue: Marietta First United Methodist Church, Marietta
blurb:
The Glatter-Gotz pipe organ at Marietta First United Methodist is the kind of instrument that makes you stop and actually listen. On Sunday afternoon, Andrew Van Varick, the church's Associate Director of Music, is presenting his first solo recital on it, which is already a milestone worth showing up for.

The program pulls from Bach, Herbert Howells, Louis Vierne, and Calvin Hampton, a genuinely interesting mix of eras and styles. If you've ever sat in a cathedral and felt the organ in your chest more than heard it, that's what this is. An hour or so on a Sunday afternoon, in a beautiful space, with serious music played live. And it's free.

For anyone who appreciates classical music or just wants a genuinely different Sunday afternoon, this one is worth the short drive.
scoring_notes: Educated, established audience with likely appreciation for classical music. The 'first recital on this organ' angle adds genuine uniqueness. Free entry removes any barrier. Sunday afternoon timing is ideal for this demographic. Niche appeal, but strong within that niche for East Cobb's older, culturally engaged residents.

event_name: The Georgia Room Presents: The Three Governors Controversy
blurb:
In 1947, Georgia somehow ended up with three people simultaneously claiming to be governor. It's one of the strangest, most uniquely Georgia stories in state history, and if you've never heard it, you're going to want the full version.

Switzer Library's Georgia Room series is bringing this one to life on Wednesday evening, November 4. It runs one hour. It's free. And it's exactly the kind of local history that sounds like something you'd make up but is completely real.

If you've got any appreciation for Southern politics, weird American history, or just great stories, this is worth an hour of your Wednesday night.
scoring_notes: Highly educated audience with likely interest in local and state history. The Three Governors Controversy is genuinely fascinating Georgia history with broad curiosity appeal. Free, low commitment, one hour. Strong fit for empty nesters and historically curious residents. Less likely to draw younger families but solid for the 40+ segment.

event_name: Matt Maher & Sarah Kroger: Cathedrals Tour
venue: St. Peter Chanel Catholic Church, Roswell
blurb:
Matt Maher is one of the most recognized names in contemporary Christian music, and he's bringing the Cathedrals Tour to St. Peter Chanel in Roswell with Sarah Kroger, which means this is a proper worship concert, not a Sunday service with better production.

If this music is part of your life, or even the periphery of it, being in a real church with live worship on a Thursday night is a different experience than a stadium. It's intimate. The setting actually matches the music. Two hours, no opener you've never heard of, just two serious artists doing what they do.

It's right down the road in Roswell. Check the website for ticketing details and grab your spot before it sells out.
scoring_notes: Matt Maher has genuine national recognition in Christian music circles. The intimate church venue setting makes this more special than a general concert. East Cobb skews toward churchgoing, community-minded families, making this a strong niche fit. Not universal appeal, but strong for a segment of this audience.

event_name: Nightmare on Main 5K
blurb:
Running a 5K on Halloween morning in a city called Kennesaw, on a course called Nightmare on Main, is objectively a fun way to start the holiday. This race is part of the Kennesaw Grand Prix series, which is USATF-certified and professionally timed, so it's a real race if you're chasing a Peachtree qualifier. But the atmosphere is also completely welcoming if you're showing up in a costume and planning to walk most of it.

The course runs through Downtown Kennesaw and Swift-Cantrell Park. It's mostly flat and fast. There's also a one-mile fun run at 7:30 AM and a Tot Trot at 8:55 if you're bringing the whole crew. At $35 with a race shirt included, it's a solid morning out before the trick-or-treat chaos begins.

If you're not registered yet, note that the shirt cutoff was October 25, so you're past that. But you can still sign up and race.
scoring_notes: Halloween timing gives a recurring race real seasonal uniqueness. Active, fitness-oriented demographic fits East Cobb's profile well. The mix of competitive timing and casual atmosphere serves both ends of this audience. Family-friendly options (fun run, tot trot) work for the established families segment.

event_name: Opera Theater Presents: The Old Maid and the Thief
blurb:
If you've never seen a comedic opera, this is a low-stakes way to find out you love them. KSU Opera Theatre is performing Gian Carlo Menotti's "The Old Maid and the Thief" at Morgan Concert Hall, and it's a one-act show, which means no three-hour commitment and no intermission confusion.

Menotti wrote this one in 1939 as a radio opera, which is already a wild and interesting origin story. The plot is essentially a farcical con job, gossip, twisted morality, and a very bad woman doing very entertaining things to a perfectly honest man. It's in English, so you won't need a libretto cheat sheet to follow along.

KSU's program consistently punches above its weight, and Morgan Concert Hall is a proper venue. If you've been meaning to give live opera a try, this is an easy entry point.
scoring_notes: Well-educated, higher-income audience with cultural curiosity. A comedic one-act opera lowers the barrier to entry significantly compared to full productions. KSU is local and respected. The English libretto and short runtime make this approachable for first-timers in this demographic.

event_name: Spooky Movies at The Strand: Hocus Pocus (1993)
blurb:
Halloween at the Strand is genuinely one of the cooler things Marietta does. They're showing Hocus Pocus on Halloween night itself, which is exactly the right movie on exactly the right night.

What makes this one worth going to instead of just pulling it up at home is the live pre-show. Thirty minutes before the film, the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ fires up for a live concert inside that beautiful old venue. There's a 3 PM showing if you want to make it a family afternoon, and an 8 PM showing if the kids are out trick-or-treating and you want something for yourself once the candy bowl is empty.

This is the kind of Halloween that doesn't require a costume or a plan. Just show up to a great old theater, watch three witch sisters terrorize Salem, and have a good time.
scoring_notes: Halloween night screening with a live organ pre-show elevates this well above a basic movie rerun. The dual showtimes serve both families with younger kids and adults/teens going separately. Strand Theatre is a real venue with genuine charm. Hocus Pocus has broad generational appeal across this audience's age range.

event_name: Fall Colors Canoe Trips
blurb:
The Chattahoochee doesn't look like this for long. Right now, the tree canopy along the river corridor is doing its full fall thing, and the Nature Center is running guided canoe trips so you can actually be in it instead of just driving past it on 400.

You'll paddle out in the late afternoon, which means golden light on the water and the kind of quiet that's genuinely hard to find around here. Wildlife tends to come out around this time of day too. It's ages 8 and up, so if you've got a teenager who needs to put the phone down for three hours, this is a solid excuse. And if it's just you and your person looking for something that isn't another restaurant, this works even better.

At $45 a head, it's nothing. Spots will fill. Go get on the water before the leaves are gone.
scoring_notes: Peak fall foliage canoe trips have a narrow seasonal window, making this genuinely time-sensitive. At $45, it's a non-issue for a $118K household. Works perfectly for the mix of established families with older kids and empty nesters who want an active, outdoor experience. The Chattahoochee Nature Center is practically in East Cobb's backyard.

event_name: Weaving Demo: The Wild Wild Weft
blurb:
The name alone deserves some credit. The Wild Wild Weft is a two-hour weaving demonstration that runs Saturday afternoon, and it's the kind of hands-on, craft-focused event that tends to be way more interesting in person than it sounds on paper.

If you've got kids who are curious about making things, or you're into fiber arts, or you just want something genuinely different from your usual Saturday afternoon, this fills a gap. It's free, it's indoors, and it's a good option to slot between the morning car show and the evening Halloween events without burning out before the main event.
scoring_notes: Lower mass appeal but high uniqueness score. Arts and crafts demos skew toward families with curious kids and creative adults. Fits the educated demographic profile (50% bachelor's degree or higher). Low stakes, low cost, and fills the afternoon gap on Saturday. Included to give variety in the lineup rather than stacking four near-identical event types.

event_name: Acoustic Jam Session
blurb:
Friday night, live acoustic music, three hours. If you need more than that to decide, you might be overthinking it.

Acoustic sets are low-key in the best way. No overwhelming volume, no cover charge, no pressure to stay for a full concert arc. You can grab dinner nearby, drift in when it's already going, and just let the weekend start the right way. This is a solid option for couples looking for something easy or a small group that wants to actually be able to have a conversation while there's music playing.

Kick the weekend off right. It's free and it starts at 6.
scoring_notes: Recurring events are generally lower priority, but this fills a Friday night adult slot that no other candidate covers. The audience skews 36 median age with dual-income households who want low-effort, low-cost weeknight options. Works for the Flower Mound and Highland Village crowd looking for something easy after the work week. Included because Friday coverage matters and this is the only Friday candidate.

event_name: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Film Screening
blurb:
Look, if you've never seen Rocky Horror in a room full of people who actually know what to do during a screening, you're missing something. This is not a movie you watch quietly. People dress up, shout callbacks at the screen, and generally commit in a way that makes a regular Saturday night at home feel embarrassing by comparison.

Halloween week is the only time of year this one really makes sense, and it's happening Saturday night. The college-adjacent crowd near UNT and TWU will feel right at home here. But honestly anyone who enjoys a little chaos with their cult classics should show up in costume and see what happens.

It starts at 8:00 PM. Come ready to participate.
scoring_notes: Seasonal uniqueness is high since Rocky Horror screenings are essentially a Halloween-only tradition. Strong fit for the younger, college-adjacent segment of the audience and adults who want something that isn't a kids event. Lower family match but that's fine since Little Monsters on Main covers that lane. Good balance in the lineup.

event_name: EsDeeKid at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb: EsDeeKid hits the Coca-Cola Roxy this Saturday night for a show that runs through 11:30pm. The Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta and it's right at The Battery, so you've got a full night if you want it: dinner before, show, and a place to land after without ever moving your car twice. This is a solid Saturday-night-out option for the crowd that wants live music without a stadium production. Doors open at 7, so get there early if you want to actually be in the room for the start.
scoring_notes: The Roxy is close to the Perimeter coverage area and The Battery is a familiar destination for this demographic. EsDeeKid is a niche pick that may not land with the full audience, but the venue and Saturday timing are strong. Included because it's the only music concert this weekend within reasonable distance.

event_name: Amp It Up Live Music Festival featuring Heart of Atlanta
blurb: Heart of Atlanta, Atlanta's top Heart tribute band, headlines a full outdoor music festival in Roswell this Saturday. The event pulls in local musicians and bands throughout the afternoon and doubles as a fundraiser for Perfect Harmony Health's music therapy scholarship program, which helps individuals with disabilities access music therapy regardless of what they can afford. So you get a great afternoon of live music and the money goes somewhere real. If you've never heard Heart played live by people who actually take it seriously, this is your chance. Roswell Junction is a good outdoor space and October weather is about as good as it gets for this kind of thing.
scoring_notes: Broad appeal, charitable angle adds depth, outdoor festival format works for families and adults alike. Heart tribute band skews slightly older which fits the 38-median-age crowd. Not the highest uniqueness but the cause component gives it more weight than a generic music festival.

event_name: Travel Abroad with the Tritone Orchestras: A Musical World Tour
blurb: The Sunday after Halloween can go one of two ways. This is the good version. Tritone Orchestras is putting on a two-hour world music tour at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center on November 1st, working through genres and musical traditions from across multiple continents in one afternoon. It's a family-friendly option that doesn't feel like you're dragging anyone anywhere, because the concept is genuinely interesting. Music from 20-something countries in a single sit-down performance is not a normal Sunday afternoon, and the Roswell Cultural Arts Center is one of the better venues in the area for this kind of thing. Grab tickets and make the day worthwhile.
scoring_notes: Family-friendly but adult-appealing, fits the mix of young families and empty nesters in the Perimeter audience. November 1st (post-Halloween Sunday) is a good slot with low competition. The world tour concept is more interesting than a standard orchestra performance, which lifts the uniqueness score.

event_name: Lumiere Lounge Jazz Talks with Trey Wright
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb: KSU Professor Trey Wright is doing something genuinely interesting at the Strand Theatre in Marietta on November 5th. It's not a concert. It's a jazz talk, 30 people max, one drink ticket included, doors at 7pm with the presentation at 7:30. This edition is on Charlie Christian and the evolution of jazz guitar, which is one of those corners of music history that feels obscure until someone walks you through it and suddenly you can't believe you didn't know it sooner. Thirty seats. Adults only (21+). The kind of Thursday night that's worth rescheduling dinner for.
scoring_notes: High education level in this audience makes a professor-led jazz history talk a genuinely good fit. 30-seat cap creates real scarcity. Adult-only format matches the more adult-skewing Perimeter audience. Thursday publish window means this lands with enough lead time to act on it.

event_name: Blacksmithing Skulls with Michael Dillon
blurb: You're going to forge an iron skull. That's the thing. Local artist Michael Dillon, known for large-scale architectural metalwork, is teaching a hands-on blacksmithing session at Art Center West in Roswell this Saturday. You'll work with raw iron, use real tools, and walk out with something you actually made with your hands. It's Halloween-adjacent in the best possible way, and it's the kind of Saturday afternoon that zero percent of your coworkers will have had. Seats are limited by the nature of the space, so if this sounds like your kind of afternoon, don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness score, skilled-instructor-led experience, Halloween timing with the skull theme. Fits the educated, experience-seeking demographic well. Lower demographic fit than bar crawl or dinner party because it's niche, but that niche is strong and the audience can afford it.

event_name: Emo Night and Halloween Party
blurb: If you spent any part of your teens or early twenties listening to My Chemical Romance or Fall Out Boy with the lights off, this one's going to hit. Rock 'N' Taco in Roswell is throwing a Halloween-themed emo night on October 29th with live throwback performances from Pop Rocks ATL. It's early enough in the week that it's not competing with Halloween Saturday, which means the crowd will be smaller and the vibe will be better. Show up in costume or don't, but either way come ready to sing every word to songs you thought you'd forgotten. Starts at 8pm.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 puts a big chunk of this audience squarely in the emo-era nostalgia zone (early 2000s). Adult-skewing, low barrier to entry, social and fun without being a massive production. The Halloween angle adds seasonal relevance.

event_name: Roswell Boos & Booze Halloween Bar Crawl
blurb: Halloween falls on a Saturday this year, which means the bar crawl situation in Roswell is going to be loud, costumed, and worth showing up for. The 3rd Annual Boos & Booze crawl runs from 3pm to 10pm through Canton Street and the surrounding spots, so you get a full evening without being locked into one venue all night. This is the kind of event that's better with a group. Round up whoever you've been meaning to make plans with, commit to a group costume, and make a night of it. Seven hours of downtown Roswell on Halloween is hard to beat.
scoring_notes: Halloween on a Saturday is a once-every-few-years occurrence that elevates what would otherwise be a recurring event. Adult-skewing, social, fits the young professional and young-family-without-kids-tonight crowd well. Roswell is close enough to Perimeter to be worth the drive for this one.

event_name: "It's Showtime!" A Beetlejuice Dinner Party
venue: Mise en Place Cooking Studio, Roswell
blurb: Halloween is five days away and this one is genuinely different. Mise en Place Cooking Studio in Roswell is throwing a hands-on dinner party inspired by Beetlejuice, and you're not just eating the food, you're making it. The whole thing is interactive, themed from start to finish, and runs just 2.5 hours so it's a real weeknight option without blowing up your Thursday morning. For a $105K household audience that's done the standard haunted house circuit about a dozen times, a cooking class where the menu is the costume is a breath of weird, fresh air. It sells out fast. Don't wait on it.
scoring_notes: High uniqueness, adult-skewing, fits the educated professional crowd that wants experiences over passive entertainment. Halloween timing is perfect for the newsletter window. Cooking studio events tend to sell limited seats, which adds genuine urgency.

event_name: Dueling Pianos at Park Bench
blurb:
No cover. No setlist. Just two pianists going at it for three hours while the crowd decides what gets played. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench in The Battery is the kind of Saturday night that starts as 'we'll just stay for one drink' and ends at midnight.

The show runs 8:30 to 11:30pm. General seating is first-come, first-served and it fills up, so if you're going with a group, reserving a table ahead of time is the smarter move. The Battery makes it easy to grab dinner somewhere first and walk over.

Free admission, good energy, and a crowd that's actually there to have fun. Hard to argue with that on a Saturday night in October.
scoring_notes: No-cover Saturday night entertainment at The Battery is very accessible for this demographic. Interactive format skews adult and social, fits young professionals well. Lower uniqueness score because Dueling Pianos is a recurring Saturday event, not a one-off. Still included because the entertainment value and zero cost are strong selling points for this audience.
